Threat.value: I am on high alert when I hear unexpected or loud sounds
Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it
I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable.
I have to be on guard all the time

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits in marked tension with 'Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time' in a severe PTSD profile. These can sometimes coexist, but as selected together here they suggest opposing levels of emotional accessibility to the trauma memory and are clinically hard to reconcile without additional context.

issues.item: Emotionless Recall: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Emotionless Recall' and 'Terror on Recall' describe opposing states during recall of the same trauma memory—detached/numb versus re-experiencing intense terror. These can both occur across different moments in PTSD, but when selected together as parallel descriptors of recall they create a direct within-node inconsistency that is hard to interpret as a single coherent memory profile without further qualification.

issues.item: Watching Others: I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me
issues.explanation: 'Watching Others' implies a current interpersonal danger schema centered on being personally harmed by others. For a patient whose index trauma was witnessing domestic violence in childhood, this is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which otherwise centers on fear/terror memories and unfairness about what happened rather than a coherent belief that other people now pose direct personal harm.

issues.item: No Accountability: The people responsible have faced no consequences
issues.explanation: 'No Accountability' and 'Injustice' fit anger/moral injury themes, but in this profile they are not well integrated with the selected threat items. The formulation's strongest active pathway is Negative Appraisals ↔ Threat, so appraisals should plausibly map onto the threat experience. These two items focus on perpetrators escaping consequences, whereas the threat node is dominated by hyperarousal to sounds and generalized surveillance of others, creating a weak clinical link.
